extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors and news organizations (particularly AP staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and principles for producing and vetting news reporting that ensure accuracy, fairness, and independence; intended as AP's guidance for journalists and newsrooms on ethical newsgathering and publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: report the news accurately and honestly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We are The Associated Press. We have a long-standing role setting the industry standard for ethics in journalism. It is our job — more than ever before — to report the news accurately and honestly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and practices to prevent bias and inaccuracies
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists at The Associated Press utilize a set of standards and practices that safeguards AP stories from bias and inaccuracies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the 'Telling the story' heading, the page emphasizes that AP journalists follow defined standards and practices designed to protect stories from bias and inaccuracies. (The page links to further detail/downloads for these standards.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: We avoid behavior or activities that create as a conflict of interest that compromise our ability to report the news fairly and accurately, uninfluenced by any person or action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AP requires staff to avoid conduct that creates conflicts of interest or the appearance of influence; the site includes a dedicated 'Conflicts of interest' section and downloadable guidance on the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to AP-specific policies and downloadable guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The page provides downloadable materials (e.g., 'News values and principles', 'Social media guidelines') that define and expand the organization's expectations for reporting and conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site points readers to downloadable documents for detailed guidance on news values, social media use, and conflicts of interest; producers/editors are expected to consult those documents for operational rules and examples.
